- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior 7-day avg), model often overshoots; cap next 3-day forecast at +5% above peak.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is rising, model underestimates continuation; add 2–5% to forecast for next 5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (especially 1–5 days ahead); apply +3% bias to first 5 forecast points.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model overfits short-term noise; smooth 3-day moving average before forecasting.
- If recent 7-day avg is rising and sentiment is neutral, model often fails to capture momentum; forecast 1–2% above recent 7-day high.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment when price is near support/resistance; if sentiment is strong and price is near recent low, forecast 1–3% above current level.
